paper_title: Self-Interpretability LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that   Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
caption: Results of Experiments 1 and 2. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini can accurately report quantitative factors driving their decision-making across a great variety of scenarios, and fine-tuning on accurate explanation further improves their ability to do so. Left: Models were making choices based on preferences instilled in them by fine-tuning. Each point corresponds to a single attribute (e.g., condo ceiling height; 5 per choice contexts, 100 choice contexts). Location in the x-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model assigned to an attribute (as reflected in their decisions). Location in the y-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model reported assigning to that attribute when prompted explicitly. The weights the models reported meaningfully correlated with the weights that actually guided their decisions, and fine-tuning on examples of accurate reports further improved their accuracy. Right: The Pearson correlation between the models' reported and learned attribute weights before and after training (blue and purple, respectively). The reports of the base models that had not undergone this fine-tuning were almost entirely uncorrelated with the learned preferences (gray). Thus, the accuracy of the fine-tuned models must reflect their ability to report their new (fine-tuned) preferences and not an informed guess about their preferences based on their general background knowledge. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs.

model_annotations.Chinese: The bar chart illustrates the self-report accuracy of GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini models in reporting the weights assigned to attributes that influenced their decision-making, comparing performance before and after introspection training. The vertical axis, labeled "Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)," is a linear scale ranging from 0.00 to 1.00, representing the correlation between the models' reported attribute weights and the actual weights instilled through fine-tuning. The horizontal axis displays two model categories: GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini. For each model, three bars are shown: a gray bar for the Control group (base models without fine-tuning), a light blue bar for the "Before Introspection Training" condition, and a dark purple bar for the "After Introspection Training" condition. The control bars for both models are near zero, indicating near-zero correlation between reported and actual preferences. In contrast, the bars for the "After Introspection Training" condition are significantly higher, with GPT-4o achieving a self-report accuracy of approximately 0.75 and GPT-4o-mini reaching about 0.76. The "Before Introspection Training" bars for both models are lower, at approximately 0.56 for GPT-4o and 0.51 for GPT-4o-mini. Error bars, representing 95% highest density intervals (HDIs), are present for all bars, with the control bars exhibiting the largest uncertainty. The data show that fine-tuning on accurate explanation examples substantially improves the models' ability to accurately report their instilled preferences.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the self-report accuracy of GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini models in reflecting their instilled preferences, comparing control conditions with performance before and after introspection training. The vertical axis, labeled "Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)," ranges from 0.00 to 1.00, representing the correlation between reported and actual attribute weights. The horizontal axis displays two model variants: GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini. For each model, three bars are shown: a gray bar for the control condition, a light blue bar for performance before introspection training, and a dark purple bar for performance after introspection training. In both models, the control accuracy is low (around 0.2 for GPT-4o and near 0.0 for GPT-4o-mini), while accuracy increases significantly after training, reaching approximately 0.75 for GPT-4o and 0.72 for GPT-4o-mini. The light blue bars (before training) show moderate accuracy, around 0.60 for GPT-4o and 0.52 for GPT-4o-mini. Error bars, representing 95% highest density intervals (HDIs), are present for all bars, indicating variability in the estimates. The results demonstrate that fine-tuning on accurate explanations improves the models' ability to report their internal decision-making processes, with the post-training reports showing strong correlations with actual preferences.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm zeigt die Selbstberichtsgenauigkeit (Instilled Preferences) für zwei Modelle, GPT-4o und GPT-4o-mini, unter drei Bedingungen: Control, Before Introspection Training und After Introspection Training. Die vertikale Achse stellt die Selbstberichtsgenauigkeit dar, mit einem Wertebereich von 0.00 bis 1.00, wobei die Beschriftungen in Schritten von 0.25 angegeben sind. Die horizontale Achse zeigt die beiden Modelle, GPT-4o und GPT-4o-mini, die in dieser Reihenfolge angeordnet sind. Für jedes Modell sind drei gruppierte Balken dargestellt, die durch Farbe und Legende unterschieden werden: grau für Control, hellblau für Before Introspection Training und dunkelblau für After Introspection Training. Die Balken für Control liegen bei GPT-4o bei etwa 0.10 und bei GPT-4o-mini bei etwa 0.05. Die Balken für Before Introspection Training erreichen bei GPT-4o etwa 0.55 und bei GPT-4o-mini etwa 0.50. Die Balken für After Introspection Training liegen bei GPT-4o bei etwa 0.75 und bei GPT-4o-mini bei etwa 0.76. Jeder Balken verfügt über eine vertikale Fehlerbalken, die die 95%-HDI (Highest Density Intervals) repräsentieren. Die Balken sind nicht alphabetisch oder nach Wert sortiert, sondern nach Modellgruppen gruppiert. Es gibt keine visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Schattierungen oder Fettdruck.
